rounds.restatement: Add a single-tag statement {{SET name = expression}} to the deterministic, no-eval template language. It binds a local to the value that the same evaluator behind ${{ }} computes. The value is kept as it is (an array stays an array). In render a math result is stored as the number the output prints. The local is visible from the tag to the end of its innermost block, is fresh on each FOR iteration and never writes the caller's data. Bad names and bad shapes are located syntax errors at parse time. Lenient mode binds null for missing data and strict mode raises a located missing-variable. The tag is standalone for whitespace, and analyze, spec() and OpenAPI agree with the new tag. The lexer keyword lookup becomes own-property only, and the one evaluator bounds the size of a text after each filter and for a SET value. Templates that were valid before keep their output and errors, except the named exceptions. No existing test expectation changes except the logged surfaces.test.ts amendment.
rounds.brief_mismatch: The card says docs_impact none and no living-document edits or deltas, but SET is a user-visible new tag. docs/living/architecture/language-contract.md still says 'SET, INPUT, CALL, macros and partials are not built yet', and its 'Surfaces that agree' section describes spec().blocks as openers with END_ closers only. The project rule says a change to a durable fact is recorded as a delta, and the card's User documentation section was left as the unfilled template (no user_visible, user_docs or waiver). The lead should either add a modify delta for the language contract (and a README/user_docs entry or waiver) or record why none is needed. This is not a finding against the build.

findings.title: Render math output now round-trips through Number(formatNumber(result)) and back to text, which can change ${{ }} math output when the formatted text is not JavaScript's shortest number form

serves.scenario: At base, visitVariable printed formatNumber(result) as is in render. Now evaluateValue returns Number(formatNumber(result)) and visitVariable prints it through valueToString/valueToText. That gives the same text only when formatNumber already emits the shortest round-trip form. If formatNumber prints an exponent-range or very large result in another form, an existing template prints a different text. The language contract says 'integers of any size ... print unchanged', and a fixed 15-significant-digit form of a tiny result is another case. Such a template was valid before, and m5 forbids any output change except the named ones. The st-compat guards cover only 7, 2.5, 0.3, Infinity and NaN.
